about: Frame bible for the frame-by-frame battle sheets (v2). One entry per archetype x motion. Plan and reasons: docs/plans/2026-11-26_motion_frames.md. Per-character overrides (timing, engine, mannequin joints): tools/art/specs/motion_chars.json. Budget and signature checker: node tools/art/requests.js --motion. When an instruction changes, edit this JSON (and motion_chars.json), not the code.

units.ms: game-clock (view clock) ms. View clock = dt x min(2, speed) x 1.3 (js/battle.js main loop), so 1x real time = ms / 1.3; at speed s > 2 one view ms lasts s/2 sim ms.
units.head: posekit head units (1 head = 110 px on the 1536x1024 source canvas, 4 heads tall, sole line y=870, hip x=192 in a 384-px frame). x is absolute (+x = facing direction), hip heights are above the floor, hand points use the posekit at() convention (h relative to the shoulder line 2.40). lean / tilt in radians (0.262 rad = 15 deg), weapon angle wa in degrees as in tools/art/handoff.py KEY_POSES.
units.src_px: pixels on the 1536x1024 source canvas; game px = src px x 0.1654 (class / most captains).

who.PC-mannequin: every frame of every attack / hit / run sequence has a mannequin (skeleton) frame made by the PC Aseprite session from this spec plus the character's motion_chars.json overrides. The cloud does not build seq8 drafts; the PC may script them itself (as walk8_pc.py) or start from the walk/run .aseprite drafts as body templates.
who.GPT-key: final art drawn by GPT on the mannequin frames (1536x1024, 1x4 strip, one strip per delivery).
who.PC-inbetween: final art made by the PC on the game-size seed: rigid moves at source size by script plus paint-under, or freehand. Freehand frames are marked elastic + droppable and are measured in the pilot before they count.
who.reuse: an already accepted cell is reused unchanged (named in motion_chars.json).

rules.budget: one attack sequence (first frame to the end of settle) must fit 0.9 x (shortest basic cd of every unit that uses the sheet) x 1000 - 30 ms; cd jitter x0.9..1.1 at js/battle.js useSkill (sk.left = sk.cd * (0.9 + r * 0.2)).
rules.fit: FAIL when the sequence does not fit even with every elastic frame at 40 %; WARN when it fits only with compression.
rules.lead: lead = ms before the contact frame starts. Each archetype has window_ms (its prediction window, <= 400). FAIL when a nominal lead exceeds window_ms. Unpredicted actions start at the contact frame, so the contact frame must read on its own.
rules.speed_conversion: at speed s > 2 the view clock runs at min(2, s)/s of the sim, so the post-contact cap 0.9 x cd - lead - 30 ms becomes (0.9 x cd - 30) x min(2, s)/s view ms (x0.5 at 4x, x0.667 at 3x). At >= 3x anticipation is skipped and playback starts at the contact frame; the protected frames (contact up to cut) must fit that converted budget (FAIL otherwise).
rules.contact: the frame on which the sim's damage / shot spawn / heal lands (release for projectiles). Exactly one contact frame per sequence, also for multi-target melee (hits > 1 land in one sim tick, js/battle.js useSkill targets.forEach strike).
rules.hold: the anticipation hold is elastic (shrinks first when the budget is short).
rules.cut: from the cut frame on, the next action or a hit may interrupt.
rules.multi_target_stagger_source: js/battle.js slash fx t: -i * 0.05 - victim reactions use the same constant, one value for slashes and reactions
rules.multi_shot: projectiles are sim objects and are never delayed: one release frame plus a fan VFX.
rules.rally: tgt:self skills (rally / shout / buff) hold the attack hold frame for 450 ms with the existing ring VFX instead of swinging at the air.
rules.heal_facing: a heal faces its target; view-side only (an r.* override in the renderer), never u.face in the sim.
rules.dx: per-frame body offset in game px at sheet scale 1; the engine multiplies by the draw scale sheetK (bosses 1.5x), as lungeOf already does with K.
rules.smear: slash smears are drawn by the engine (drawSmear), never painted into frames.
rules.guide_similarity: two characters' mannequin frames (hold and contact at game size, alpha IoU) above 0.8 = the same template = FAIL (requests.js --motion). Characters sharing a base set must carry different overrides.

rules.banned_note: 'kick' alone is NOT banned: recoil wording such as 'arm kicks up' (Marisol's pistol) is legitimate.

hit.about: Hit sequences by weight. Reading comes from the silhouette first: head and shoulders snap away and return, knees absorb, feet planted (one stagger step at most for light), weapon kept, face changes (wince / eyes shut / teeth gritted) but a ~10 px face barely reads at 96 px. Heavy characters rock less. Joint values are the hit job's posekit.HIT_KEYS (tools/pixelart/posekit.py, 5beb7f6) and the limits are handoff.py HIT_RULES; posekit / handoff win if they differ - update this copy.
hit.retrigger: a new hit within 200 ms of the current hit's start does not restart the sequence: it re-shows K1 for its ms and resumes where it was (heavy: ignored). Hits interrupt idle, run and attack frames from cut on; they never interrupt an attack before its contact.

heavy.users: DEFAULT only, for sheets not in motion_chars.json hit.sheets (the one source of a sheet's weight): the archetypes whose hit_default is heavy (greatweapon, chain, big). Typical: braced defenders and big monsters / bosses.

humanoid.pilot_note: Pilot: the rest key plus today's sprite-gen breathing loop (offline). The three cloth-lag in-betweens are NOT made in the pilot (a 1 px breathing change does not read at 64-75 px; C6).

humanoid.played_by: distance, not time (js/battle.js gaitUpdate r.rp / pose run branch): one step = min(runStride x sheetK, code stride strideOf). The ms are nominal (80 ms at the code cadence of about 3 steps/s at 1x).
humanoid.gate: No run strip goes out before runStride per run class is fixed with the run job (C8). run_base/v1 has 45.5 game px, about twice a warrior's code stride, so drawn feet slide about 6 px per cell. In the pilot S3/S4 come after the attack and hit strips.

runStride_game_px_est.about: estimate from strideOf at the class speed (CLASS_STATS warrior 24, rogue 34, archer 26, mage 22, cleric 24; MONSTER_STATS 27): stride ~ 20.6 x clamp((speed/25)^0.75, 0.85, 1.4) game px for a ~66 px body. The run job measures and fixes the real values.

humanoid.owner_of_anims_run: v2 sheets: the v2 row layout (seed .aseprite, row 1) owns anims.run; registering a v2 sheet drops its sheet.gaits record so re-registration cannot duplicate it. Old 7-cell sheets keep the add_gait.py append + sheet.gaits re-attach path until they convert (S7).

melee_swing.contact_rule: slash / chop: weapon angle crosses the strike line; thrust: weapon tip at its furthest reach; shield shove: shield face at its furthest reach
melee_swing.weapon_outside_silhouette: hold and contact: >= 60 % of weapon pixels over magenta, tip >= 33 src px outside the body

bow.note: SPEC 8 bow exception (stands upright; the wind-up is the draw length). The release must move the string hand >= 60 src px back from the hold (the weakest-reading contact today) and carry the origin mark.

gun.note: fire -> recoil reads by the weapon bucking up and the shoulders rocking back

cast.note: staff tip / palm / mace head travels >= 100 src px from hold to release toward the target; the origin mark sits on that focus
